# sngl:remote/http declares `get` and leaves it open — what an HTTP request *is*
# is not a question any tier below a target can answer. sngl:language/go closes
# it with an override whose body calls a declaration marked #[go.native], and
# the whole chain has to arrive at the Go package that performs the request.
#
# Every link is load-bearing and each has been broken on its own: the language
# package not loading at all, the override merging into nothing, and the native
# call rendering as the SNGL name because only a namespace-qualified call site
# consulted the mark.

sngl generate --lang go --platform bubbletea --out out app.sngl

# The transport, spelled as Go spells it after the import.
grep 'http\.Get\(' out/model.go
grep 'git\.duckfam\.us/jonathan/sngl/pkg/go/remote/http' out/model.go

# The name the SNGL declaration carries is not a name anything in Go declares:
# a native declaration *is* the foreign identifier rather than corresponding to
# one, so nothing emits it under its own name.
! grep 'httpGet' out/model.go

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:app"
import http "sngl:remote/http"

component main {
    var url = "https://example.com/"

    window(title="get") {
        text(value=http.get(url).body)
    }
}

output(lang="go", platform="bubbletea")
